meta.description: Provides an interactive screen for bank administrators to browse, search, select, and initiate updates or deletions of Transaction Type reference data records.
meta.process_description: This CICS online program presents a paginated list of Transaction Type codes and their descriptions from the TRANSACTION_TYPE reference table, allowing administrators to browse up to 7 records per screen page. Users can filter the list by transaction type code or description, then select individual records for update (action code 'U') or deletion (action code 'D'). Only one action may be selected at a time; selecting a record for update navigates to the COTRTUPC update program, while deletion requires confirmation via F10 before the record is removed. The program enforces data integrity by validating user input, detecting changes, and providing informational messages to guide the user through each step of the maintenance workflow.

files.TRANSACTION_TYPE (DB2 Table): Reference table holding all valid transaction type codes and their business descriptions used across the credit card system
files.COTRTLI (Mapset): BMS screen map definition for the transaction type list display screen (CTRTLIA)
files.COTRTUP (Mapset): BMS screen map definition for the transaction type update/add screen, navigated to when an update action is selected

business_rules: Only one action (update or delete) may be selected at a time across all displayed rows; selecting more than one triggers an error message 'Please select only 1 action'.
Valid action codes are strictly 'U' (update) or 'D' (delete); any other non-blank entry is rejected with 'Action code selected is invalid'.
A deletion requires explicit confirmation by pressing F10 after the record is highlighted; the record is not deleted on initial selection alone.
An update action navigates the user to the COTRTUPC program (transaction CTTU) passing the selected transaction type code for editing.
If no records match the current search/filter criteria, the message 'No records found for this search condition.' is displayed and no action is permitted.
If the user attempts to save an update but no data has actually changed compared to the database values, the system rejects the save with 'No change detected with respect to database values.'
The screen displays a maximum of 7 transaction type records per page; paging is implemented using DB2 cursors with a start key to support forward navigation through the reference table.
Filter criteria (type code and/or description) can be combined to narrow search results; changes to filter values reset the paging position.
The program enforces that transaction type descriptions are non-blank and contain only valid alphanumeric characters before allowing an update to be saved.
Upon successful deletion or update, a confirmation message is displayed and the list is refreshed to reflect the current state of the reference table.

variables.name: WS-CONSTANTS
variables.description: Group record holding all fixed system constants used by the Transaction Type List program, such as program names, transaction IDs, map names, and action flag values that never change at runtime.

variables.name: LIT-THISPGM
variables.description: The CICS program name of this Transaction Type List program itself ('COTRTLIC'). Used when registering the current program in the communication area so that other programs know which program is currently executing and can return to it correctly.

variables.name: LIT-THISTRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction ID ('CTLI') associated with this Transaction Type List screen. Used when re-invoking or returning to this screen so CICS knows which transaction to start.

variables.name: LIT-THISMAPSET
variables.description: The BMS mapset name ('COTRTLI') that contains the screen layout definitions for the Transaction Type List display. Used when sending or receiving the list screen to/from the terminal.

variables.name: LIT-THISMAP
variables.description: The specific BMS map name ('CTRTLIA') within the COTRTLI mapset that defines the layout of the Transaction Type List screen. Used to send the correct screen panel to the administrator's terminal.

variables.name: LIT-ADMINPGM
variables.description: The program name of the Administration Menu ('COADM01C') that the user is returned to when they exit the Transaction Type List screen. Represents the parent menu in the administrative navigation hierarchy.

variables.name: LIT-ADMINTRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction ID ('CA00') for the Administration Menu program. Used when transferring control back to the admin menu so CICS starts the correct transaction.

variables.name: LIT-ADMINMAPSET
variables.description: The BMS mapset name ('COADM01') belonging to the Administration Menu program. Used when navigating back to the admin menu so the correct screen layout is displayed.

variables.name: LIT-ADDTPGM
variables.description: The program name of the Transaction Type Update/Add program ('COTRTUPC'). When an administrator selects a transaction type record for update (action 'U'), control is transferred to this program to allow editing of the record's details.

variables.name: LIT-ADDTTRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction ID ('CTTU') for the Transaction Type Update program. Used when transferring control to the update screen after the administrator selects a record for editing.

variables.name: LIT-ADDTMAPSET
variables.description: The BMS mapset name ('COTRTUP') for the Transaction Type Update screen. Used when navigating to the update program so the correct screen layout is loaded for editing a transaction type record.

variables.name: LIT-ADDTMAP
variables.description: The specific BMS map name ('CTRTUPA') within the COTRTUP mapset that defines the layout of the Transaction Type Update/Add screen. Used to display the correct edit panel when an administrator opens a transaction type record for modification.

variables.name: LIT-DSNTIAC
variables.description: The name of the IBM DB2 SQLCA message formatting utility program ('DSNTIAC'). Used to translate DB2 error codes into human-readable messages when a database operation on the Transaction Type table fails.

variables.name: LIT-ASTERISK
variables.description: A literal asterisk character ('*') used as a wildcard or visual marker on the Transaction Type List screen, for example to indicate a selected or highlighted row to the administrator.

variables.name: LIT-TRANTYPE-TABLE
variables.description: The DB2 table name for the Transaction Type reference table. Used in dynamic SQL or error messages to identify which database table is being queried or updated when browsing and maintaining transaction type codes.

variables.name: LIT-DELETE-FLAG
variables.description: The system constant 'D' representing a delete action request. When an administrator enters 'D' next to a transaction type record on the list screen, this constant is used to identify and process the deletion request.

variables.name: LIT-UPDATE-FLAG
variables.description: The system constant 'U' representing an update action request. When an administrator enters 'U' next to a transaction type record on the list screen, this constant is used to identify and route the user to the update program.

variables.name: WS-MAX-SCREEN-LINES
variables.description: The maximum number of transaction type records displayed per page on the list screen (7 rows). Controls how many records are fetched from the DB2 Transaction Type table per page and limits the number of rows the administrator can interact with at one time.

variables.name: LIT-ALL-ALPHANUM-FROM-X
variables.description: Group record containing the full set of valid alphanumeric characters (uppercase letters, lowercase letters, and digits) used as a reference for input validation. Ensures that transaction type descriptions entered by administrators contain only acceptable characters.

variables.name: LIT-ALL-ALPHA-FROM-X
variables.description: Sub-group containing the full set of valid alphabetic characters (uppercase and lowercase letters) used when validating that a transaction type description contains only letters.

variables.name: LIT-UPPER
variables.description: All 26 uppercase alphabetic characters (A–Z) used as the valid uppercase reference set when validating that a transaction type description or code contains only acceptable alphabetic characters.

variables.name: LIT-LOWER
variables.description: All 26 lowercase alphabetic characters (a–z) used as the valid lowercase reference set when validating that a transaction type description entered by an administrator contains only acceptable alphabetic characters.

variables.name: LIT-NUMBERS
variables.description: All 10 numeric digit characters (0–9) used as the valid numeric reference set when validating that a transaction type description or code contains only acceptable numeric characters.

variables.name: LIT-ALL-ALPHA-FROM
variables.description: A 52-character working field (26 uppercase + 26 lowercase) used as the source reference string in INSPECT or string validation operations to confirm that transaction type descriptions contain only valid alphabetic characters.

variables.name: LIT-ALL-ALPHANUM-FROM
variables.description: A 62-character working field (26 uppercase + 26 lowercase + 10 digits) used as the source reference string in validation operations to confirm that transaction type descriptions entered by administrators contain only valid alphanumeric characters.

variables.name: LIT-ALL-NUM-FROM
variables.description: A 10-character working field containing all digit characters (0–9) used as the source reference string when validating that a transaction type code or numeric field contains only valid numeric characters.

variables.name: LIT-ALPHA-SPACES-TO
variables.description: A 52-character target field filled with spaces, used as the destination in INSPECT CONVERTING operations to effectively strip or count non-alphabetic characters when validating transaction type description input.

variables.name: LIT-ALPHANUM-SPACES-TO
variables.description: A 62-character target field filled with spaces, used as the destination in INSPECT CONVERTING operations to detect invalid characters when validating that a transaction type description contains only alphanumeric characters.

variables.name: LIT-NUM-SPACES-TO
variables.description: A 10-character target field filled with spaces, used as the destination in INSPECT CONVERTING operations when validating that a transaction type code or numeric field contains only valid digit characters.

variables.name: WS-MISC-STORAGE
variables.description: Group record containing miscellaneous working-storage fields used during the processing of the Transaction Type List screen, including CICS response codes, input validation flags, filter change indicators, and action status flags.

variables.name: WS-CICS-PROCESSNG-VARS
variables.description: Group of variables used to capture and evaluate CICS command responses during screen I/O and program control operations, ensuring that any CICS errors encountered while displaying the Transaction Type List are detected and handled.

variables.name: WS-RESP-CD
variables.description: The CICS response code returned after each CICS command (such as sending a screen or reading a map). A non-zero value indicates a CICS error occurred during the Transaction Type List screen operation, triggering error handling.

variables.name: WS-REAS-CD
variables.description: The CICS reason code providing additional detail about why a CICS command failed. Used alongside WS-RESP-CD to diagnose and log specific CICS errors encountered while processing the Transaction Type List screen.

variables.name: WS-TRANID
variables.description: A working field holding the CICS transaction ID to be used when transferring control to another program (such as the update program or admin menu). Set dynamically based on the administrator's action before issuing a CICS XCTL or RETURN command.

variables.name: WS-INPUT-FLAG
variables.description: Overall input validation status flag for the current screen interaction. Indicates whether all user inputs on the Transaction Type List screen (filters, action codes) have passed validation checks before processing proceeds.

variables.name: INPUT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that all user inputs on the Transaction Type List screen are valid and processing can proceed (e.g., action codes are valid, filters are acceptable).

variables.name: INPUT-ERROR
variables.description: Condition indicating that one or more user inputs on the Transaction Type List screen have failed validation (e.g., invalid action code, multiple actions selected), causing an error message to be displayed and processing to be halted.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-TYPE-FLAG
variables.description: Validation status flag for the transaction type code filter field entered by the administrator. Tracks whether the type code filter value is blank, valid, or invalid, controlling whether the filter can be applied to narrow the list of transaction types.

variables.name: FLG-TYPEFILTER-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the transaction type code filter value entered by the administrator has failed validation and cannot be used to search the Transaction Type reference table.

variables.name: FLG-TYPEFILTER-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the transaction type code filter value entered by the administrator has passed validation and can be used to filter the list of transaction type records displayed on screen.

variables.name: FLG-TYPEFILTER-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator has left the transaction type code filter field blank, meaning no filtering by type code will be applied and all transaction type records will be eligible for display.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-DESC-FLAG
variables.description: Validation status flag for the transaction type description filter field entered by the administrator. Tracks whether the description filter value is blank, valid, or invalid, controlling whether it can be applied to narrow the list of transaction types shown.

variables.name: FLG-DESCFILTER-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the transaction type description filter value entered by the administrator has failed validation and cannot be used to search the Transaction Type reference table.

variables.name: FLG-DESCFILTER-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the transaction type description filter value entered by the administrator has passed validation and can be used to filter the list of transaction type records displayed on screen.

variables.name: FLG-DESCFILTER-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator has left the description filter field blank, meaning no filtering by description will be applied and all transaction type records will be eligible for display.

variables.name: WS-TYPEFILTER-CHANGED
variables.description: Flag indicating whether the administrator has changed the transaction type code filter value since the last screen interaction. When changed, the paging position is reset so the list restarts from the beginning of the filtered results.

variables.name: FLG-TYPEFILTER-CHANGED-NO
variables.description: Condition indicating that the transaction type code filter has not been changed by the administrator since the last screen display, so the current paging position can be maintained.

variables.name: FLG-TYPEFILTER-CHANGED-YES
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator has modified the transaction type code filter, requiring the list to be re-queried from the beginning of the matching records rather than continuing from the previous page position.

variables.name: WS-DESCFILTER-CHANGED
variables.description: Flag indicating whether the administrator has changed the transaction type description filter value since the last screen interaction. When changed, the paging position is reset so the list restarts from the beginning of the filtered results.

variables.name: FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-NO
variables.description: Condition indicating that the transaction type description filter has not been changed by the administrator since the last screen display, so the current paging position can be maintained.

variables.name: FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-YES
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator has modified the description filter, requiring the list to be re-queried from the beginning of the matching records rather than continuing from the previous page position.

variables.name: WS-ROW-RECORDS-CHANGED
variables.description: Per-row flag (array) tracking whether the administrator has modified the description of a displayed transaction type record. Used to detect actual data changes before allowing an update to be saved, preventing unnecessary database writes when no real change has been made.

variables.name: FLG-ROW-DESCR-CHANGED-NO
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator has not changed the description of this particular transaction type row, so no update needs to be saved for this record.

variables.name: FLG-ROW-DESCR-CHANGED-YES
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator has modified the description of this particular transaction type row, signalling that the change should be validated and saved to the Transaction Type reference table.

variables.name: WS-DELETE-STATUS
variables.description: Flag indicating whether the deletion of the selected transaction type record has been successfully completed. When set to 'Y', the program displays a deletion confirmation message and refreshes the list to reflect the removal of the record from the reference table.

variables.name: FLG-DELETED-NO
variables.description: Condition indicating that no deletion of a transaction type record has been completed in the current interaction, so no deletion confirmation message needs to be displayed.

variables.name: FLG-DELETED-YES
variables.description: Condition indicating that the selected transaction type record has been successfully deleted from the reference table. Triggers display of a success confirmation message and a refresh of the transaction type list.

variables.name: WS-UPDATE-STATUS
variables.description: Flag indicating whether an update to the selected transaction type record has been successfully completed. When set to 'Y', the program displays an update confirmation message and refreshes the list to reflect the saved changes in the reference table.

variables.name: FLG-UPDATED-NO
variables.description: Condition indicating that no update to a transaction type record has been completed in the current interaction, so no update confirmation message needs to be displayed.

variables.name: FLG-UPDATE-COMPLETED
variables.description: Condition indicating that the selected transaction type record has been successfully updated and saved to the reference table. Triggers display of a success confirmation message and a refresh of the transaction type list to show the updated description.

variables.name: WS-ROW-SELECTION-CHANGED
variables.description: Tracks whether the administrator has changed their action selection (U/D) on any row compared to what was previously displayed. Used to detect if the user has altered which transaction type record they want to act upon between screen interactions.

variables.name: FLG-ROW-SELECTION-CHANGED-NO
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator has NOT changed their row selection since the last screen interaction. The action selection remains the same as before, so no re-evaluation of the chosen transaction type record is needed.

variables.name: FLG-ROW-SELECTION-CHANGED-YES
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator HAS changed their row selection since the last screen interaction. The system must re-evaluate which transaction type record is now targeted for update or deletion.

variables.name: WS-BAD-SELECTION-ACTION
variables.description: Flag indicating whether the administrator has entered an invalid action code in any of the selection fields on the transaction type list screen. An invalid action is anything other than 'U' (update) or 'D' (delete).

variables.name: FLG-BAD-ACTIONS-SELECTED-NO
variables.description: Condition indicating that all action codes entered by the administrator are valid (either blank, 'U', or 'D'). Processing can continue without displaying an invalid action error message.

variables.name: FLG-BAD-ACTIONS-SELECTED-YES
variables.description: Condition indicating that at least one action code entered by the administrator is invalid (not 'U', 'D', or blank). The system will reject the request and display the error message 'Action code selected is invalid'.

variables.name: WS-ARRAY-DESCRIPTION-FLGS
variables.description: Validation status flag for a transaction type description field being edited by the administrator. Indicates whether the description entered is valid, blank, or contains invalid characters before allowing an update to be saved.

variables.name: FLG-ROW-DESCRIPTION-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the transaction type description entered by the administrator has passed all validation checks — it is non-blank and contains only valid alphanumeric characters. The update may proceed.

variables.name: FLG-ROW-DESCRIPTION-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the transaction type description entered by the administrator contains invalid characters (non-alphanumeric). The system will reject the update and prompt the administrator to correct the description.

variables.name: FLG-ROW-DESCRIPTION-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the transaction type description field has been left blank by the administrator. Since a description is mandatory for every transaction type record, the system will reject the update and require a non-blank value.

variables.name: WS-DATACHANGED-FLAG
variables.description: Flag indicating whether the administrator has actually modified any transaction type data compared to the values currently stored in the database. Prevents a meaningless save operation if nothing has changed, enforcing the business rule that rejects updates with 'No change detected with respect to database values.'

variables.name: NO-CHANGES-FOUND
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator has not actually changed any transaction type description compared to what is stored in the database. The system will reject the save attempt and display 'No change detected with respect to database values.'

variables.name: CHANGES-HAVE-OCCURRED
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator has genuinely modified at least one transaction type description compared to the database value. The system will allow the update to proceed and save the new description to the TRANSACTION_TYPE reference table.

variables.name: WS-GENERIC-EDITS
variables.description: Group of working storage fields used as a shared workspace for performing generic data validation routines. These fields are reused across different edit checks (e.g., validating transaction type descriptions) to avoid duplicating validation logic.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-VARIABLE-NAME
variables.description: The name of the field currently being validated, used to produce meaningful error messages. For example, when validating a transaction type description, this would hold the label 'Transaction Type Description' so the error message identifies which field failed validation.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-ONLY
variables.description: Temporary holding area for the data value being validated for alphanumeric content. When checking a transaction type description, the description text is moved here so the generic validation routine can inspect it for invalid characters.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-LENGTH
variables.description: The length of the data value being validated for alphanumeric content. Tells the generic validation routine how many characters of WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-ONLY to inspect, allowing the same routine to validate fields of different sizes (e.g., a 50-character transaction type description).

variables.name: WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-ONLY-FLAGS
variables.description: Result flag returned by the generic alphanumeric validation routine after inspecting a field value. Indicates whether the validated field (e.g., transaction type description) is valid, blank, or contains invalid non-alphanumeric characters.

variables.name: FLG-ALPHNANUM-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the field being validated contains only valid alphanumeric characters. For a transaction type description, this means the text is acceptable and the update can proceed.

variables.name: FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the field being validated contains at least one invalid non-alphanumeric character. For a transaction type description, the system will reject the update and prompt the administrator to correct the entry.

variables.name: FLG-ALPHNANUM-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the field being validated is entirely blank. For a transaction type description, a blank value is not permitted, and the system will reject the update requiring the administrator to provide a meaningful description.

variables.name: WS-OTHER-EDIT-VARS
variables.description: Group of additional working storage variables used during data editing and validation operations on the transaction type list screen.

variables.name: WS-RECORDS-COUNT
variables.description: Running count of transaction type records retrieved from the TRANSACTION_TYPE table for the current page. Used to determine whether any records matched the search criteria and how many rows to display on the list screen (up to the maximum of 7).

variables.name: WS-SCREEN-DATA-IN
variables.description: Group structure holding all transaction type data received from the list screen (CTRTLIA) after the administrator submits the screen. Contains the transaction type codes and descriptions as entered or displayed across all 7 rows.

variables.name: WS-ALL-ROWS-IN
variables.description: Flat character buffer holding the combined screen input data for all 7 transaction type rows (7 rows × 52 characters per row = 364 bytes). Provides a single contiguous view of all row data received from the screen, used as the base for the structured row array redefinition.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Structural redefinition of the flat screen input buffer that overlays it with a structured 7-row array. Allows the program to access each transaction type row's code and description individually rather than as a single flat string.

variables.name: WS-SCREEN-ROWS-IN
variables.description: Array of 7 entries, each representing one row of transaction type data as received from the list screen. Corresponds to the maximum of 7 transaction type records displayed per page, allowing the program to process each row's input individually.

variables.name: WS-EACH-ROW-IN
variables.description: Container for all screen input fields belonging to a single transaction type row on the list screen. Groups the transaction type code and description for one displayed record as entered by the administrator.

variables.name: WS-EACH-TTYP-IN
variables.description: Sub-group holding the specific transaction type data fields (code and description) for one row received from the screen. Provides a named grouping for the two key data elements of a transaction type reference record.

variables.name: WS-ROW-TR-CODE-IN
variables.description: The 2-character transaction type code for one row as received from the list screen. This is the unique identifier for a transaction type in the TRANSACTION_TYPE reference table (e.g., 'SA' for Sale, 'RE' for Refund). Used to identify which record the administrator is acting upon.

variables.name: WS-ROW-TR-DESC-IN
variables.description: The 50-character business description of the transaction type for one row as received from the list screen. This is the human-readable label for the transaction type code (e.g., 'Sale Transaction'). Validated for non-blank alphanumeric content before any update is saved to the TRANSACTION_TYPE table.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-SELECT-COUNTER
variables.description: Loop counter used when iterating through the 7 action selection fields on the screen to count and validate the action codes (U/D) entered by the administrator across all displayed transaction type rows.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-SELECT-FLAGS
variables.description: Flat 7-character string holding the action codes entered by the administrator for all 7 displayed transaction type rows. Each character position corresponds to one row's action selection ('U' for update, 'D' for delete, or blank for no action). Serves as the base for the structured array redefinition.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Structural redefinition of the flat action selection string that overlays it with a 7-element array. Allows the program to access and validate each row's action code individually using an index.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-SELECT
variables.description: The action code entered by the administrator for one specific transaction type row on the list screen. Valid values are 'U' to request an update or 'D' to request a deletion of that transaction type record. Blank means no action is requested for that row.

variables.name: SELECT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the action code entered for a row is one of the two valid choices: 'D' (delete) or 'U' (update). Used to confirm the administrator has entered a recognized action before processing the request.

variables.name: DELETE-REQUESTED-ON
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator has entered 'D' for this row, requesting deletion of the corresponding transaction type record. Deletion requires subsequent confirmation via F10 before the record is actually removed from the TRANSACTION_TYPE table.

variables.name: UPDATE-REQUESTED-ON
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator has entered 'U' for this row, requesting an update of the corresponding transaction type record. The system will navigate to the COTRTUPC program (transaction CTTU) passing the selected transaction type code for editing.

variables.name: SELECT-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator has left the action selection field blank for this row, meaning no action is requested for that particular transaction type record. Blank rows are ignored during action processing.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-SELECT-ERROR-FLAGS
variables.description: Flat 7-character string holding error indicators for the action selection fields across all 7 displayed rows. Each character position flags whether the corresponding row's action code is invalid. Serves as the base for the structured error flag array redefinition.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Structural redefinition of the flat error flag string that overlays it with a 7-element array. Allows the program to set and check error indicators for each row's action selection field individually.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-SELECT-ERRORS
variables.description: Array of 7 error indicator entries, one per displayed transaction type row. Each entry records whether the action code entered for that row is invalid, enabling the screen to highlight specific rows where the administrator made an invalid selection.

variables.name: WS-ROW-TRTSELECT-ERROR
variables.description: Error indicator for the action selection field of one specific transaction type row. When set to '1', signals that the administrator entered an invalid action code for this row, triggering the error message 'Action code selected is invalid' and highlighting the offending field on screen.

variables.name: WS-ROW-SELECT-ERROR
variables.description: Condition indicating that the action code entered for this specific transaction type row is invalid. When true, the system will flag this row on the screen and display an error message instructing the administrator to use only 'U' or 'D' as valid action codes.

variables.name: WS-SUBSCRIPT-VARS
variables.description: Group of loop index variables used to iterate through the 7 rows of transaction type data displayed on the list screen during validation and processing operations.

variables.name: I
variables.description: General-purpose loop index used to iterate through the 7 displayed transaction type rows when validating action codes, counting selections, or processing screen input data row by row.

variables.name: I-SELECTED
variables.description: Index recording which specific row number (1–7) the administrator has selected for an update or delete action. Used to retrieve the correct transaction type code and description from the screen data arrays when processing the chosen record.

variables.name: WS-ACTIONS-SELECTED
variables.description: Group of counters that tally the different types of actions entered by the administrator across all 7 displayed transaction type rows. Used to enforce the business rule that exactly one action may be selected at a time.

variables.name: WS-ACTIONS-REQUESTED
variables.description: Total count of action codes (U or D) entered by the administrator across all 7 displayed transaction type rows. Must equal exactly 1 for the system to proceed; if more than 1 is entered, the error 'Please select only 1 action' is displayed.

variables.name: WS-ONLY-1-ACTION
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator has selected exactly one action across all displayed rows. This is the required state for the system to process the request — either navigating to the update screen or initiating the delete confirmation flow.

variables.name: WS-MORETHAN1ACTION
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator has selected more than one action across the displayed rows. This violates the business rule requiring exactly one selection, and the system will display the error 'Please select only 1 action'.

variables.name: WS-DELETES-REQUESTED
variables.description: Count of 'D' (delete) action codes entered by the administrator across all 7 displayed transaction type rows. Used to determine whether the current action is a deletion, which requires F10 confirmation before the record is removed from the TRANSACTION_TYPE table.

variables.name: WS-UPDATES-REQUESTED
variables.description: Count of 'U' (update) action codes entered by the administrator across all 7 displayed transaction type rows. Used to determine whether the current action is an update, which triggers navigation to the COTRTUPC program for editing the selected transaction type record.

variables.name: WS-NO-ACTIONS-SELECTED
variables.description: Count of rows where the administrator left the action selection field blank, indicating no action is requested for those transaction type records. When all 7 rows are blank, no processing is performed and the screen is simply refreshed.

variables.name: WS-VALID-ACTIONS-SELECTED
variables.description: Count of valid action codes (strictly 'U' or 'D') entered by the administrator across all displayed rows. Distinguishes between total actions entered and those that are actually valid, helping the system differentiate between 'too many actions' and 'invalid action code' error conditions.

variables.name: WS-ONLY-1-VALID-ACTION
variables.description: Condition indicating that exactly one valid action code ('U' or 'D') has been entered by the administrator. Combined with WS-ONLY-1-ACTION, confirms that the single action entered is also a recognized valid code, allowing processing to proceed.

variables.name: CICS-OUTPUT-EDIT-VARS
variables.description: Group of working storage variables used when preparing output data for CICS screen display or program-to-program communication, particularly for formatting the transaction type code before sending it to the update program or displaying it on screen.

variables.name: TRAN-TYPE-CD-X
variables.description: The 2-character transaction type code of the record selected by the administrator for update or deletion, held as a character string. This is the key value passed to the COTRTUPC program when navigating to the update screen, identifying which TRANSACTION_TYPE record to edit.

variables.name: TRAN-TYPE-CD-N
variables.description: Numeric redefinition of the 2-character transaction type code, allowing the code to be interpreted or validated as a numeric value when needed. Provides an alternative numeric view of the same transaction type code field for arithmetic or numeric comparison operations.

variables.name: FLG-PROTECT-SELECT-ROWS
variables.description: Flag controlling whether the action selection fields on the transaction type list screen are protected (read-only) or open for input. When a delete confirmation or update is pending, the selection fields may be protected to prevent the administrator from changing their selection mid-process.

variables.name: FLG-PROTECT-SELECT-ROWS-NO
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the action selection fields (U/D) on each displayed transaction type row are currently open for user input — the administrator is allowed to type an action code next to any listed record.

variables.name: FLG-PROTECT-SELECT-ROWS-YES
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the action selection fields on each displayed transaction type row are locked/protected from user input — typically set after an action has been selected and is awaiting confirmation (e.g., pending delete confirmation via F10), preventing the user from changing their selection mid-flow.

variables.name: WS-LONG-MSG
variables.description: A large working-storage buffer used to assemble extended diagnostic or informational text during processing — for example, building a detailed DB2 error description or concatenating multiple message segments before displaying or logging them.

variables.name: WS-INFO-MSG
variables.description: The short informational guidance message displayed at the bottom of the transaction type list screen to instruct the administrator what action to take next (e.g., 'Press F10 to confirm deletion' or 'Press F10 to save update'). Its current state is tested via the 88-level conditions below.

variables.name: WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE
variables.description: Condition indicating that no guidance message is currently active on the screen — the info message area is blank, meaning the administrator has not yet selected any action that requires a follow-up instruction.

variables.name: WS-INFORM-REC-ACTIONS
variables.description: Condition indicating that the screen is currently showing a general prompt instructing the administrator to select an action (U to update or D to delete) against one of the displayed transaction type records.

variables.name: WS-INFORM-DELETE
variables.description: Condition indicating that the screen is currently displaying the delete confirmation prompt — the administrator has selected 'D' on a transaction type record and is being instructed to press F10 to confirm and permanently remove that transaction type from the reference table.

variables.name: WS-INFORM-UPDATE
variables.description: Condition indicating that the screen is currently displaying the update save prompt — the administrator has selected 'U' on a transaction type record and is being instructed to press F10 to confirm and save the modified transaction type description to the database.

variables.name: WS-INFORM-DELETE-SUCCESS
variables.description: Condition indicating that the info message area is showing a successful deletion confirmation — the selected transaction type record has been permanently removed from the reference table and the administrator is being notified of the successful outcome.

variables.name: WS-INFORM-UPDATE-SUCCESS
variables.description: Condition indicating that the info message area is showing a successful update confirmation — the transaction type description has been saved to the database and the administrator is being notified that the change was applied successfully.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-MSG
variables.description: The primary status or error message displayed to the administrator on the transaction type list screen — communicates outcomes such as 'No records found', 'Please select only 1 action', or 'Invalid action code', guiding the user to correct their input or understand the result of their last action.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF
variables.description: Condition indicating that no status or error message is currently being shown to the administrator — the message area is clear, meaning the last operation completed without any issue requiring user attention.

variables.name: WS-EXIT-MESSAGE
variables.description: Condition indicating that the screen is displaying a farewell or exit message — typically shown when the administrator navigates away from the transaction type list back to the administration menu, confirming the session on this screen has ended.

variables.name: WS-MESG-NO-RECORDS-FOUND
variables.description: Condition indicating that the message 'No records found for this search condition.' is currently displayed — the administrator's filter criteria (type code or description) did not match any transaction type records in the reference table, so no rows are shown and no actions can be taken.

variables.name: WS-MESG-NO-MORE-RECORDS
variables.description: Condition indicating that the message informing the administrator there are no further transaction type records beyond the current page is being displayed — the administrator has paged to the end of the reference table and no additional records exist to scroll forward to.

variables.name: WS-MESG-MORE-THAN-1-ACTION
variables.description: Condition indicating that the error message 'Please select only 1 action' is currently displayed — the administrator entered action codes (U or D) against more than one transaction type row simultaneously, which violates the business rule that only a single action may be processed at a time.

variables.name: WS-MESG-INVALID-ACTION-CODE
variables.description: Condition indicating that the error message 'Action code selected is invalid' is currently displayed — the administrator typed a character other than 'U' or 'D' in an action selection field, which is not a recognised operation for transaction type records.

variables.name: WS-MESG-NO-CHANGES-DETECTED
variables.description: Condition indicating that the error message 'No change detected with respect to database values.' is currently displayed — the administrator attempted to save an update to a transaction type description but the value entered is identical to what is already stored in the database, so no write is performed.

variables.name: WS-PFK-FLAG
variables.description: A flag that records whether the function key pressed by the administrator is one that the transaction type list screen recognises and supports. Used to gate processing so that unrecognised key presses are rejected with an appropriate message.

variables.name: PFK-VALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the function key pressed by the administrator (e.g., Enter, F3, F7, F8, F10) is a valid, supported key for the transaction type list screen and that processing should continue normally.

variables.name: PFK-INVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the function key pressed by the administrator is not recognised or supported by the transaction type list screen — the system will display an error and re-present the screen without performing any data operation.

variables.name: WS-STRING-FORMAT-VARS
variables.description: A group of working variables used internally when the program needs to build or manipulate text strings — for example, when constructing a DB2 SQL filter string from the administrator's search criteria or assembling a formatted message.

variables.name: WS-STRING-MID
variables.description: A numeric work counter tracking the current middle or intermediate position within a string being assembled — used as a pointer or offset when concatenating parts of a search filter or message text.

variables.name: WS-STRING-LEN
variables.description: A numeric work counter holding the current length of a string being built — used to track how many characters have been placed into the output buffer so far when constructing a filter clause or formatted message.

variables.name: WS-STRING-OUT
variables.description: The output buffer that holds the assembled text string after concatenation — for example, the formatted search filter value or a composed message segment ready to be placed on the screen or passed to a DB2 query.

variables.name: WS-DATA-FILTERS
variables.description: A group structure holding all the search and paging control values that govern which transaction type records are retrieved from the database and displayed on the current screen page — encompasses the start key for paging, the type code filter, the description filter, and the set of type codes currently displayed for potential deletion.

variables.name: WS-START-KEY
variables.description: The transaction type code that marks the beginning of the current page of results — acts as a DB2 cursor anchor so that when the administrator pages forward, the system knows which record to start reading from next, enabling correct forward navigation through the reference table.

variables.name: WS-TYPE-CD-FILTER
variables.description: The transaction type code search filter entered by the administrator — when populated, restricts the list of displayed transaction types to only those whose type code matches or starts with this value, allowing the administrator to quickly locate a specific code in the reference table.

variables.name: WS-TYPE-DESC-FILTER
variables.description: The transaction type description search filter entered by the administrator — when populated, restricts the displayed list to only those transaction types whose business description contains or matches this text, enabling keyword-based lookup of transaction type records.

variables.name: WS-TYPE-CD-DELETE-FILTER
variables.description: A structured group that holds the set of transaction type codes currently visible on the screen, formatted for use in a DB2 IN-clause or similar filter — used during delete confirmation processing to identify exactly which record the administrator has selected for removal.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A structural padding byte at the start of the delete filter group — used to align the data structure correctly, with no direct business meaning.

variables.name: WS-TYPE-CD-DELETE-FILTER-X
variables.description: The repeating portion of the delete filter structure that holds up to 7 transaction type code entries — one for each row that can appear on the screen — enabling the program to track which specific type codes are currently displayed and eligible for deletion.

variables.name: WS-TYPE-CD-DELETE-KEYS
variables.description: An array of 7 entries, one per screen row, each holding the transaction type code of the record displayed on that row — used to map the administrator's row-level delete selection back to the correct transaction type code in the database when confirming a deletion.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Padding byte before each transaction type code entry in the delete key array — used for structural alignment within the repeating group, with no direct business meaning.

variables.name: WS-TYPE-CD-DELETE-KEY
variables.description: The two-character transaction type code for a single screen row, stored within the delete key array — identifies the specific transaction type record that the administrator has highlighted for deletion on that row, used to issue the correct DB2 DELETE statement upon F10 confirmation.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Padding byte after the transaction type code within each delete key array entry — used for structural alignment, with no direct business meaning.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Additional padding byte within each delete key array entry — used for structural alignment, with no direct business meaning.

variables.name: WS-DUMMY
variables.description: A placeholder group appended after the 7 repeating delete key entries — used to complete the fixed-length structure of the delete filter area, ensuring correct byte alignment when the array has fewer than the maximum entries populated.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Padding byte within the dummy trailing group — structural filler with no direct business meaning.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Padding byte within the dummy trailing group — structural filler with no direct business meaning.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Padding byte within the dummy trailing group — structural filler with no direct business meaning.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Trailing padding byte at the end of the delete filter structure — used for structural alignment, with no direct business meaning.

variables.name: WS-SCREEN-EDIT-VARS
variables.description: A group of working variables used to hold and validate the transaction type code and description values as entered or edited by the administrator on the screen — serves as the staging area for input validation before any database update is attempted.

variables.name: WS-IN-TYPE-CD
variables.description: The two-character transaction type code as entered or selected by the administrator on the screen — holds the code of the transaction type record being acted upon (updated or deleted) before it is validated and passed to the database operation.

variables.name: WS-IN-TYPE-CD-N
variables.description: A numeric reinterpretation of the transaction type code field — allows the program to perform numeric validation checks on the entered type code (e.g., verifying it contains only digits) without altering the original character value stored in WS-IN-TYPE-CD.

variables.name: WS-IN-TYPE-DESC
variables.description: The business description of the transaction type as entered or modified by the administrator on the screen — holds the new or existing description text that will be validated for non-blank content and valid characters before being saved to the TRANSACTION_TYPE reference table.

variables.name: WS-ROW-NUMBER
variables.description: A numeric counter used during screen processing loops to track which row (1 through 7) of the displayed transaction type list is currently being examined — used to iterate over the visible records when checking for action selections, validating input, or populating screen fields.

variables.name: WS-RECORDS-TO-PROCESS-FLAG
variables.description: A control flag that governs the DB2 read loop when fetching transaction type records from the database — signals whether the program should continue reading more records or stop, enabling the program to correctly fill the 7-row screen page and detect end-of-data conditions.

variables.name: READ-LOOP-EXIT
variables.description: Condition indicating that the DB2 record fetch loop should stop — either because all 7 screen rows have been filled with transaction type records, no more records match the filter criteria, or an end-of-table condition has been reached.

variables.name: MORE-RECORDS-TO-READ
variables.description: Condition indicating that the DB2 record fetch loop should continue — more transaction type records matching the current filter criteria are available to be read and placed into the next available screen row.

variables.name: WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA
variables.description: The communication area (COMMAREA) used by this transaction type list program to pass data between CICS interactions — holds the currently selected transaction type code and description, as well as a snapshot of all 7 screen rows, so that state is preserved across screen refreshes, paging operations, and navigation to the update program.

variables.name: WS-CA-TYPE-CD
variables.description: The two-character transaction type code of the record currently selected by the administrator — passed in the COMMAREA to the update program (COTRTUPC) when the administrator chooses to update a transaction type, identifying which record is to be edited.

variables.name: WS-CA-TYPE-CD-N
variables.description: A numeric reinterpretation of the selected transaction type code in the COMMAREA — allows numeric validation or comparison of the type code value without changing the character representation passed to the downstream update program.

variables.name: WS-CA-TYPE-DESC
variables.description: The business description of the currently selected transaction type, carried in the COMMAREA — passed alongside the type code to the update program so that the administrator can see and modify the existing description when editing a transaction type record.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A group structure within the COMMAREA that holds the screen row data for all 7 displayed transaction type records — preserves the full current page of results across CICS interactions so the screen can be accurately re-displayed after paging, action selection, or error correction without re-querying the database unnecessarily.

variables.name: WS-CA-ALL-ROWS-OUT
variables.description: A flat 364-byte character field in the COMMAREA representing the combined output data for all 7 transaction type rows currently displayed on the screen — used as a single contiguous block for storage and transmission of the full page of results between CICS interactions.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A structured reinterpretation of the flat 364-byte row output area — breaks the single character block into 7 individually addressable screen row records, allowing the program to access each transaction type row's data fields independently by row index.

variables.name: WS-CA-SCREEN-ROWS-OUT
variables.description: An array of 7 entries in the COMMAREA, one for each row of the transaction type list screen — each entry holds the output data for a single displayed transaction type record, enabling the program to save and restore the full screen page across CICS interactions.

variables.name: WS-CA-EACH-ROW-OUT
variables.description: The data container for a single transaction type row's output fields within the COMMAREA array — groups together all the displayable attributes of one transaction type record (such as type code and description) so they can be stored and retrieved as a unit for each screen row.

variables.name: WS-CA-ROW-TR-CODE-OUT
variables.description: The two-character transaction type code stored in the COMMAREA for a specific screen row — records which transaction type code was displayed on that row during the last screen interaction, used to detect changes, validate actions, and correctly identify the target record for update or delete operations.

variables.name: WS-CA-ROW-TR-DESC-OUT
variables.description: The business description of a transaction type as it will be displayed to the administrator on the list screen. This 50-character field holds the human-readable label (e.g., 'Purchase', 'Cash Advance', 'Balance Transfer') for each transaction type row shown in the browse list, allowing administrators to identify and act on the correct record.

variables.name: WS-CA-ROW-SELECTED
variables.description: The row number (1–7) of the transaction type record that the administrator has selected for an update or delete action on the current screen page. This identifies which specific transaction type entry the administrator intends to act upon when multiple records are displayed simultaneously.

variables.name: WS-CA-PAGING-VARIABLES
variables.description: A group of fields that collectively manage the paging state of the transaction type list screen. These variables track which page of results is currently displayed, where the page starts and ends in the reference table, and whether more pages exist — enabling the administrator to navigate forward through large sets of transaction type records.

variables.name: WS-CA-LAST-TTYPEKEY
variables.description: The DB2 cursor key representing the last transaction type code displayed on the current screen page. This anchor point is used to determine the boundary of the current page and supports backward navigation or re-fetching logic when the administrator pages through the transaction type reference table.

variables.name: WS-CA-LAST-TR-CODE
variables.description: The two-character transaction type code of the last record shown on the current page of the browse list. This code serves as the ending boundary key for the current page, used by the paging logic to know where the current page ends in the TRANSACTION_TYPE reference table.

variables.name: WS-CA-FIRST-TTYPEKEY
variables.description: The DB2 cursor key representing the first transaction type code displayed on the current screen page. This anchor point marks the starting position of the current page and is used to re-display the same page or support navigation logic when the administrator is browsing the transaction type reference table.

variables.name: WS-CA-FIRST-TR-CODE
variables.description: The two-character transaction type code of the first record shown on the current page of the browse list. This code serves as the starting boundary key for the current page, allowing the system to re-fetch and re-display the correct set of records when the screen is refreshed after an action such as a deletion or update.

variables.name: WS-CA-SCREEN-NUM
variables.description: The current page number being displayed to the administrator in the transaction type browse list. This single-digit counter tracks which page of results the administrator is viewing, enabling the system to correctly position the DB2 cursor and display the appropriate subset of transaction type records.

variables.name: CA-FIRST-PAGE
variables.description: A condition name that is true when the administrator is viewing the very first page of the transaction type list. When active, this condition signals that no previous page exists and backward navigation should be suppressed, ensuring the administrator cannot page before the beginning of the reference table.

variables.name: WS-CA-LAST-PAGE-DISPLAYED
variables.description: A flag indicating whether the last available page of transaction type records has already been shown to the administrator. This controls whether the 'Next Page' option is offered on screen, preventing the administrator from attempting to page beyond the end of the TRANSACTION_TYPE reference table.

variables.name: CA-LAST-PAGE-SHOWN
variables.description: A condition name that is true when the final page of transaction type records has already been displayed to the administrator. When active, the system suppresses the forward-paging option, informing the administrator that there are no more transaction type records to browse beyond the current page.

variables.name: CA-LAST-PAGE-NOT-SHOWN
variables.description: A condition name that is true when the final page of transaction type records has NOT yet been reached. When active, the system allows the administrator to continue paging forward through the TRANSACTION_TYPE reference table to view additional records.

variables.name: WS-CA-NEXT-PAGE-IND
variables.description: An indicator flag that signals whether additional transaction type records exist beyond the current page. The system sets this after each DB2 fetch to determine whether a 'Next Page' navigation option should be presented to the administrator on the list screen.

variables.name: CA-NEXT-PAGE-NOT-EXISTS
variables.description: A condition name that is true when there are no further transaction type records beyond the current page. When active, the system hides or disables the forward-paging option, indicating to the administrator that the current page is the last page of the transaction type reference table.

variables.name: CA-NEXT-PAGE-EXISTS
variables.description: A condition name that is true when at least one more page of transaction type records exists beyond what is currently displayed. When active, the system enables the forward-paging option, allowing the administrator to navigate to the next set of transaction type records.

variables.name: WS-CA-DELETE-FLAG
variables.description: A state flag that tracks the lifecycle of a delete action for a transaction type record across screen interactions. It records whether a deletion has been requested by the administrator (awaiting F10 confirmation) or has been successfully completed, driving the appropriate confirmation messages and screen refresh behavior.

variables.name: CA-DELETE-NOT-REQUESTED
variables.description: A condition name that is true when no deletion of a transaction type record is currently pending. This is the default resting state, indicating the administrator has not yet selected a record for deletion on the current screen interaction.

variables.name: CA-DELETE-REQUESTED
variables.description: A condition name that is true when the administrator has selected a transaction type record for deletion (entered 'D') but has not yet confirmed the action by pressing F10. The system uses this state to display the confirmation prompt and highlight the selected record, enforcing the two-step deletion safety rule.

variables.name: CA-DELETE-SUCCEEDED
variables.description: A condition name that is true after a transaction type record has been successfully deleted from the TRANSACTION_TYPE reference table. Note: this shares the LOW-VALUES value with CA-DELETE-NOT-REQUESTED, meaning the flag is reset to its base state after a successful deletion, and the success outcome is communicated via a separate confirmation message on screen.

variables.name: WS-CA-UPDATE-FLAG
variables.description: A state flag that tracks the lifecycle of an update action for a transaction type record across screen interactions. It records whether an update has been requested by the administrator (navigating to the update screen) or has been successfully saved, driving the appropriate confirmation messages and screen refresh behavior.

variables.name: CA-UPDATE-NOT-REQUESTED
variables.description: A condition name that is true when no update of a transaction type record is currently in progress. This is the default resting state, indicating the administrator has not yet selected a record for update on the current screen interaction.

variables.name: CA-UPDATE-REQUESTED
variables.description: A condition name that is true when the administrator has selected a transaction type record for update (entered 'U') and the system is in the process of navigating to the COTRTUPC update program. This state signals that the selected transaction type code should be passed to the downstream update screen.

variables.name: CA-UPDATE-SUCCEEDED
variables.description: A condition name that is true after a transaction type record's description has been successfully saved to the TRANSACTION_TYPE reference table. Note: this shares the LOW-VALUES value with CA-UPDATE-NOT-REQUESTED, meaning the flag resets to its base state after a successful update, and the success outcome is communicated via a separate confirmation message on screen.

variables.name: WS-COMMAREA
variables.description: The raw communication area buffer used to pass data between CICS programs during navigation. This 2000-byte field holds the serialized state of the transaction type list screen — including paging position, selected record, filter criteria, and action flags — so that context is preserved when the administrator navigates to the update program (COTRTUPC) and returns, or when the screen is re-entered after a delete confirmation.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A reserved padding area at the beginning of the CTRTLIAI BMS map input structure. This filler covers the fixed header portion of the screen map (titles, filter fields, and other non-row screen elements) that precede the repeating transaction type data rows, ensuring correct byte alignment when reading user input from the screen.

variables.name: WS-ROW-DATAI
variables.description: The input data area for all 7 transaction type rows displayed on the list screen. This group field captures everything the administrator has entered or that was displayed across the 7 rows — action selection codes, transaction type codes, and descriptions — as received from the BMS map when the administrator presses a key.

variables.name: EACH-ROWI
variables.description: A repeating structure representing one row of transaction type data on the list screen, occurring 7 times to match the maximum page size. Each occurrence corresponds to one transaction type record displayed to the administrator, containing the action selection field, the type code, and the type description as received from the screen.

variables.name: TRTSELL
variables.description: The BMS-generated length attribute for the action selection field of a transaction type row. This technical field indicates how many characters the administrator actually typed into the action code field (e.g., 'U' or 'D') for this row, used by the program to detect whether any input was provided.

variables.name: TRTSELF
variables.description: The BMS-generated attribute byte for the action selection field of a transaction type row. This byte controls the visual presentation of the selection field on the screen (e.g., protected, highlighted, or normal) and reflects the field's current display state as returned from the terminal.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A REDEFINES overlay on the action selection field's attribute byte, providing an alternative named access path (TRTSELA) to the same byte. This is a standard BMS map pattern allowing the program to read the attribute byte value directly.

variables.name: TRTSELA
variables.description: The attribute byte of the action selection field for a transaction type row, accessed via the REDEFINES of TRTSELF. The program uses this to programmatically set or read the display attributes (e.g., making the field bright or protected) of the action code entry area for each row on the list screen.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A BMS map padding field between the action selection attribute byte and the action selection input value for a transaction type row. This filler maintains correct byte alignment within the BMS map structure and has no direct business meaning.

variables.name: TRTSELI
variables.description: The actual action code entered by the administrator for a specific transaction type row on the list screen. This single character captures the administrator's intent: 'U' to update the transaction type record or 'D' to delete it. The program validates this value and enforces the rule that only one action may be selected across all 7 rows.

variables.name: TRTTYPL
variables.description: The BMS-generated length attribute for the transaction type code field of a row. This technical field indicates how many characters are present in the type code field as returned from the screen, used for input validation and processing of the transaction type code value.

variables.name: TRTTYPF
variables.description: The BMS-generated attribute byte for the transaction type code field of a row. This byte controls the visual display characteristics of the type code column on the list screen (e.g., whether it is protected from editing, highlighted, or normal intensity).

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A REDEFINES overlay on the transaction type code field's attribute byte, providing an alternative named access path (TRTTYPA) to the same byte. This is a standard BMS map pattern for programmatic attribute manipulation.

variables.name: TRTTYPA
variables.description: The attribute byte of the transaction type code field for a row, accessed via the REDEFINES of TRTTYPF. The program uses this to control the display attributes of the type code column — for example, protecting it from user modification since type codes are system-defined reference values that should not be changed on the list screen.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A BMS map padding field between the transaction type code attribute byte and the type code input value for a row. This filler maintains correct byte alignment within the BMS map structure and has no direct business meaning.

variables.name: TRTTYPI
variables.description: The two-character transaction type code value for a specific row on the list screen, as received from the BMS map input. This is the unique identifier of the transaction type record (e.g., 'PU' for Purchase, 'CA' for Cash Advance) that the administrator can select for update or deletion.

variables.name: TRTYPDL
variables.description: The BMS-generated length attribute for the transaction type description field of a row. This technical field indicates how many characters are present in the description field as returned from the screen, used to detect whether the administrator has modified the description text for a transaction type record.

variables.name: TRTYPDF
variables.description: The BMS-generated attribute byte for the transaction type description field of a row. This byte controls the visual display characteristics of the description column on the list screen, such as whether it is editable or protected, and whether it is highlighted to draw the administrator's attention to a selected record.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A REDEFINES overlay on the transaction type description field's attribute byte, providing an alternative named access path (TRTYPDA) to the same byte. This is a standard BMS map pattern for programmatic attribute manipulation of the description column.

variables.name: TRTYPDA
variables.description: The attribute byte of the transaction type description field for a row, accessed via the REDEFINES of TRTYPDF. The program uses this to dynamically control the display of the description column — for example, highlighting the description of a record selected for deletion to visually confirm to the administrator which record will be affected.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A BMS map padding field between the transaction type description attribute byte and the description input value for a row. This filler maintains correct byte alignment within the BMS map structure and has no direct business meaning.

variables.name: TRTYPDI
variables.description: The 50-character business description of a transaction type as entered or displayed on the list screen, received from the BMS map input. This is the human-readable label for the transaction type (e.g., 'Purchase Transaction', 'Cash Advance') that the administrator can read to identify records and that may be modified via the update function. The program validates this field for non-blank content and valid alphanumeric characters before saving any changes.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A reserved padding area at the end of the CTRTLIAI BMS map input structure. This filler covers the fixed footer portion of the screen map (error messages, function key prompts, and other non-row screen elements) that follow the 7 repeating transaction type data rows, ensuring correct byte alignment when reading user input from the screen.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A reserved padding area at the beginning of the CTRTLIAO BMS map output structure. This filler covers the fixed header portion of the screen map (titles, filter fields, and other non-row screen elements) that precede the repeating transaction type data rows, ensuring correct byte alignment when writing output data to the screen.

variables.name: EACH-ROWO
variables.description: A repeating output structure representing one row of transaction type data sent to the list screen, occurring 7 times to match the maximum page size. Each occurrence controls the visual presentation of one transaction type record displayed to the administrator, including color, protection, and highlighting attributes for the action selection, type code, and description fields.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A BMS map padding field at the start of each output row structure. This filler covers the length and flag bytes that precede the attribute byte of the action selection field in the BMS output map, maintaining correct byte alignment for the output row data sent to the terminal.

variables.name: TRTSELC
variables.description: The color attribute for the action selection field of a transaction type output row. The program sets this to control the color in which the action code entry area is displayed on the administrator's terminal — for example, using a different color to highlight a row that has been selected for deletion or update.

variables.name: TRTSELP
variables.description: The protection attribute for the action selection field of a transaction type output row. The program sets this to control whether the administrator can type into the action code field for this row — for example, protecting all rows except those eligible for selection, or protecting the field after an action has been confirmed.

variables.name: TRTSELH
variables.description: The highlighting attribute for the action selection field of a transaction type output row. The program sets this to visually emphasize the action code field of a selected row — for example, making it blink or appear in reverse video to draw the administrator's attention to the record pending confirmation of a delete or update action.

variables.name: TRTSELV
variables.description: The validation attribute for the action selection field of a transaction type output row. This BMS extended attribute controls whether the field requires mandatory input from the administrator, used to enforce that an action code must be entered when the system expects a response from the user.

variables.name: TRTSELO
variables.description: The output value of the action selection field for a transaction type row sent to the screen. The program populates this with the current action code (e.g., 'U' or 'D') to redisplay the administrator's selection after screen processing, providing visual feedback that the entered action has been recognized and is being processed.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A BMS map padding field between the action selection output value and the transaction type code attribute fields in the output row structure. This filler covers the length and flag bytes of the type code field in the BMS output map, maintaining correct byte alignment.

variables.name: TRTTYPC
variables.description: The color attribute for the transaction type code field of an output row. The program sets this to control the color in which the two-character type code (e.g., 'PU', 'CA') is displayed on the administrator's terminal, potentially using different colors to distinguish selected records or to indicate the current state of the browse list.

variables.name: TRTTYPP
variables.description: The protection attribute for the transaction type code field of an output row. The program sets this to prevent the administrator from modifying the transaction type code directly on the list screen, since type codes are system-defined reference identifiers that can only be managed through the dedicated add/update program (COTRTUPC).

variables.name: TRTTYPH
variables.description: The highlighting attribute for the transaction type code field of an output row. The program sets this to visually emphasize the type code of a selected record — for example, displaying it in reverse video or bright intensity when the administrator has chosen that record for update or deletion, making it clear which transaction type is about to be acted upon.

variables.name: TRTTYPV
variables.description: Screen attribute/validation flag for the Transaction Type Code field on the list screen. Controls whether the transaction type code column is visible, protected, or in error state — used by BMS to visually signal to the administrator whether the type code entry is valid or requires attention.

variables.name: TRTTYPO
variables.description: The displayed Transaction Type Code value shown in a row on the list screen. This is the short reference code (e.g., 'PU', 'RF') that uniquely identifies a transaction type in the CardDemo system, presented to the administrator for browsing and selection.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Unused padding bytes between the Transaction Type Code and the Transaction Type Description fields on the screen map row. Ensures correct column alignment of the description field as displayed to the bank administrator on the transaction type list screen.

variables.name: TRTYPDC
variables.description: BMS screen attribute character for the Transaction Type Description field in a list row. Controls the display characteristics (e.g., protected, bright, dark) of the description column, allowing the system to highlight or protect the description when a record is selected for update or deletion.

variables.name: TRTYPDP
variables.description: BMS extended attribute byte (program symbol or color) for the Transaction Type Description field in a list row. Used to visually distinguish the description field — for example, highlighting a selected record's description in a different color to draw the administrator's attention during update or delete confirmation.

variables.name: TRTYPDH
variables.description: BMS extended highlight attribute for the Transaction Type Description field in a list row. Controls visual emphasis (e.g., underline, blink, reverse video) applied to the description when the administrator selects a transaction type record for update or deletion, providing clear on-screen feedback.

variables.name: TRTYPDV
variables.description: Screen validation/visibility flag for the Transaction Type Description field in a list row. Indicates to BMS whether the description field content is valid and should be displayed normally, or whether it should be flagged visually to alert the administrator to a data entry or validation error.

variables.name: TRTYPDO
variables.description: The displayed Transaction Type Description value shown in a row on the list screen. This is the human-readable business description of a transaction type (e.g., 'Purchase', 'Refund', 'Cash Advance') that helps the bank administrator understand the purpose of each transaction type code when browsing, searching, or selecting records for update or deletion.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Trailing padding bytes at the end of the BMS screen map structure (COTRTLI mapset). Fills out the remainder of the fixed-length screen communication area to the required total length, ensuring correct memory alignment and data integrity when the screen map is passed between CICS and the COTRTLIC program.

variables.name: DFHCOMMAREA
variables.description: The CICS Communication Area (COMMAREA) passed between programs during transaction navigation. In COTRTLIC, this area carries session context — including user identity, program routing information, and state flags — as the administrator navigates between the transaction type list screen, the update program (COTRTUPC), and the administration menu (COADM01C). It is the primary mechanism for maintaining state across screen interactions in the stateless CICS environment.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Placeholder byte within the CICS COMMAREA definition.
