Reserves the minimum required space in the communication area structure, ensuring the COMMAREA is recognized and correctly mapped by CICS when the program is first entered or re-entered during the transaction type list management workflow.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN
paragraphs.description: This is the main orchestration paragraph for the Transaction Type maintenance screen. It initialises the session, interprets the administrator's key presses and action selections, and routes processing to the appropriate business function: paging through records, navigating to the update program, confirming deletions, or returning to the administration menu.

paragraphs.name: COMMON-RETURN
paragraphs.description: Finalises the current user interaction cycle by recording the identity of this screen and program in the shared session context, then suspends the Transaction Type list program and hands control back to CICS, ready to re-enter the same screen on the next user action (e.g. a key press or selection).

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the formal exit point of the main processing routine for the Transaction Type maintenance screen. This paragraph serves as the structural boundary that concludes the top-level workflow orchestration for the COTRTLIC program.

paragraphs.name: 1000-RECEIVE-MAP
paragraphs.description: Orchestrates the capture and validation of administrator input from the Transaction Type list screen, collecting any filter criteria, paging requests, and action selections (update/delete) entered by the user, then verifying that all entries meet business rules before any maintenance action is processed.

paragraphs.name: 1000-RECEIVE-MAP-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the end of the screen input reception routine, serving as the exit point after all user-entered data (filters, action codes, paging keys) has been captured from the transaction type list screen.

paragraphs.name: 1100-RECEIVE-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Captures the administrator's input from the Transaction Type list screen, transferring all entered filter criteria, action codes, and any modified descriptions into working storage for subsequent validation and processing.

paragraphs.name: 1100-RECEIVE-SCREEN-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the screen data reception routine, marking the end of the process that captures and interprets administrator input from the Transaction Type list screen.

paragraphs.name: 1200-EDIT-INPUTS
paragraphs.description: Orchestrates the full validation of all user inputs entered on the Transaction Type list screen, ensuring that action selections, descriptions, type codes, and combined filter criteria are all individually and collectively valid before any maintenance action is permitted to proceed.

paragraphs.name: 1200-EDIT-INPUTS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the formal exit point of the input validation routine (1200-EDIT-INPUTS), allowing control to return to the calling paragraph after all user-entered action codes and filter criteria have been validated.

paragraphs.name: 1210-EDIT-ARRAY
paragraphs.description: Validates the action codes entered by the administrator across all displayed transaction type rows, ensuring exactly one valid action (update or delete) has been selected before any maintenance operation can proceed. It also detects invalid action codes, flags rows in error, and tracks whether the user's row selection has changed since the last screen interaction.

paragraphs.name: 1210-EDIT-ARRAY-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the formal end of the user input validation routine that checks action codes entered by administrators for transaction type records. Serves as the exit point that returns control to the calling paragraph after all action code edits have been completed.

paragraphs.name: 1211-EDIT-ARRAY-DESC
paragraphs.description: Validates whether the administrator has actually modified a transaction type description for a given row, and if so, ensures the new description contains only valid alphanumeric characters and is non-blank before allowing the update to proceed.

paragraphs.name: 1211-EDIT-ARRAY-DESC-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the transaction type description validation routine. It marks the end of the description editing logic, returning control to the calling paragraph after all description field validations have been completed.

paragraphs.name: 1220-EDIT-TYPECD
paragraphs.description: Validates the transaction type code filter entered by the administrator before applying it to the reference data search. Ensures the filter is either left blank (no filtering) or contains a valid 2-digit numeric code, rejecting any non-numeric input with a descriptive error message.

paragraphs.name: 1220-EDIT-TYPECD-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Detects whether the administrator has changed the transaction type code filter criterion. If the filter has changed, the paging position is reset so the list restarts from the beginning with the new search criteria applied.

paragraphs.name: 1230-EDIT-DESC
paragraphs.description: Validates and prepares the transaction type description filter entered by the administrator. If a description filter value was provided, it is formatted as a SQL wildcard pattern to enable partial-match searching against the reference table.

paragraphs.name: 1230-EDIT-DESC-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Detects whether the administrator has changed the description filter field compared to the previously active filter. If a change is detected, the paging position is reset and the new filter value is saved so the transaction type list will be refreshed from the beginning using the updated search criteria.

paragraphs.name: 1240-EDIT-ALPHANUM-REQD
paragraphs.description: Validates that a required transaction type description field is neither blank nor contains invalid characters, ensuring only alphanumeric values are accepted before allowing an update to be saved to the reference table.

paragraphs.name: 1240-EDIT-ALPHANUM-REQD-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the alphanumeric validation routine that verifies transaction type descriptions contain only valid characters. It marks the end of the validation subroutine, returning control to the calling business logic after the description field check is complete.

paragraphs.name: 1290-CROSS-EDITS
paragraphs.description: Validates that the user's active filter criteria (type code and/or description) actually return matching records from the Transaction Type reference table. If no records are found, the screen is locked from accepting any actions and the user is informed to revise their search.

paragraphs.name: 1290-CROSS-EDITS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: 1290-CROSS-EDITS-EXIT marks the end of the cross-validation routine for user input. 2000-SEND-MAP orchestrates the full preparation and delivery of the Transaction Type list screen to the administrator, coordinating all screen setup steps before rendering the display.

paragraphs.name: 2000-SEND-MAP-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the formal end of the screen-sending routine, serving as a structured exit point that returns control to the calling paragraph after the transaction type list screen has been presented to the administrator.

paragraphs.name: 2100-SCREEN-INIT
paragraphs.description: Initialises the Transaction Type list screen with standard header information, current date/time, page number, and a cleared message area, preparing a clean display for the administrator before any data is loaded or user interaction begins.

paragraphs.name: 2100-SCREEN-INIT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the formal exit point of the screen initialisation routine, allowing the program to return control to the calling paragraph after the Transaction Type list screen has been prepared for display.

paragraphs.name: 2200-SETUP-ARRAY-ATTRIBS
paragraphs.description: Configures the visual display attributes (protection, colour, cursor position, editability) for each of the 7 transaction type rows on the list screen, reflecting the current state of each row — whether it is empty, selected for deletion, selected for update, or contains a validation error — so the screen guides the administrator through the correct next action.

paragraphs.name: 2200-SETUP-ARRAY-ATTRIBS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the screen attribute setup routine (2200-SETUP-ARRAY-ATTRIBS), which configures the display properties of the transaction type list rows. It acts as a structured return marker, allowing any internal logic within the routine to branch here cleanly when setup is complete.

paragraphs.name: 2300-SCREEN-ARRAY-INIT
paragraphs.description: Populates each row of the transaction type list screen with the appropriate transaction code, description, and action selection indicator, applying business rules around pending delete/update confirmations and data change detection before rendering the display.

paragraphs.name: 2300-SCREEN-ARRAY-INIT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the formal exit point of the screen array initialisation routine, which prepares the on-screen rows for displaying transaction type records. This paragraph serves as a structured termination label, allowing the program to cleanly return control after the screen display data has been set up.

paragraphs.name: 2400-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS
paragraphs.description: Configures the visual presentation and cursor positioning of the Transaction Type search filter fields on the list screen, applying appropriate colours, protection states, and cursor focus based on the current user interaction context (first entry, action selection, filter validation status, or error conditions).

paragraphs.name: 2400-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the formal end boundary of the screen attribute setup routine (2400-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS). This is a structural exit point that allows the program to cleanly return control after configuring the display properties of the transaction type list screen.

paragraphs.name: 2500-SETUP-MESSAGE
paragraphs.description: Determines and formats the appropriate status or guidance message to display to the administrator based on the outcome of their last action (deletion, update, paging, or record selection), then renders that message centered on the transaction type list screen.

paragraphs.name: 2500-SETUP-MESSAGE-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the end of the message setup routine, serving as a structural exit point that returns control to the calling workflow step after all user guidance or error messages have been prepared for display.

paragraphs.name: 2600-SEND-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Renders and displays the Transaction Type list maintenance screen to the bank administrator, presenting the current page of transaction type records with any applied filters, action selections, and guidance messages. This is the final step in each interaction cycle, making the updated screen visible to the user.

paragraphs.name: 2600-SEND-SCREEN-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the formal end boundary of the screen-sending routine for the Transaction Type list screen. This is a structural termination point that allows the program to cleanly exit the send-screen logic and return control to the calling paragraph.

paragraphs.name: 8000-READ-FORWARD
paragraphs.description: Retrieves the next page of Transaction Type reference records from the database to populate the administrator's browse screen, loading up to 7 records per page and determining whether further pages of records exist for forward navigation.

paragraphs.name: 8000-READ-FORWARD-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the formal end of the forward-paging read routine that retrieves the next page of Transaction Type records. Serves as a structural exit point, ensuring control returns cleanly to the calling logic after the page of up to 7 records has been loaded.

paragraphs.name: 8100-READ-BACKWARDS
paragraphs.description: Navigates backward through the Transaction Type reference table to populate the previous page of results, filling up to 7 records in reverse order so the administrator can page back through the list. This supports the backward paging workflow by reading records preceding the current page's starting key and assembling them into the correct display sequence.

paragraphs.name: 8100-READ-BACKWARDS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Finalises the backward paging operation by closing the reverse-direction DB2 cursor used to navigate to a previous page of Transaction Type records, ensuring database resources are released cleanly after the backward scroll is complete.

paragraphs.name: 9100-CHECK-FILTERS
paragraphs.description: Validates the administrator's search filter criteria by counting how many Transaction Type records in the reference table match the entered type code and/or description filters. This count determines whether any matching records exist before the screen is populated, preventing unnecessary navigation or empty result displays.

paragraphs.name: 9100-CHECK-FILTERS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the formal exit point of the filter validation routine, allowing the program to return control to the calling paragraph after all filter criteria checks have been completed.

paragraphs.name: 9200-UPDATE-RECORD
paragraphs.description: Persists the administrator's approved changes to a Transaction Type description in the reference table, then commits the change to the database or raises an appropriate error message if the update fails due to a missing record, a database conflict, or another database error.

paragraphs.name: 9200-UPDATE-RECORD-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the formal exit point of the transaction type record update processing routine. This paragraph serves as a structured termination boundary for the 9200-UPDATE-RECORD section, ensuring controlled return to the calling workflow after all update validation and processing steps have completed.

paragraphs.name: 9300-DELETE-RECORD
paragraphs.description: Permanently removes a selected Transaction Type reference record from the database after the administrator has confirmed the deletion. Handles referential integrity violations and other database errors by providing appropriate guidance messages to the user.

paragraphs.name: 9300-DELETE-RECORD-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the formal exit point of the transaction type record deletion routine, allowing the program to cleanly return control to the calling paragraph after all deletion processing steps have been completed.

paragraphs.name: 9400-OPEN-FORWARD-CURSOR
paragraphs.description: Opens the DB2 database cursor that will retrieve Transaction Type reference records in forward order, starting from the current page position. If the cursor cannot be opened, the paragraph captures the database error details to inform the administrator that the reference data list cannot be displayed.

paragraphs.name: 9400-OPEN-FORWARD-CURSOR-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This is a formal exit point paragraph that marks the end of the forward cursor opening routine used to begin paginated retrieval of Transaction Type records from the database. It serves as a structured termination label, allowing other parts of the program to transfer control here after the cursor has been opened for browsing.

paragraphs.name: 9450-CLOSE-FORWARD-CURSOR
paragraphs.description: Closes the active DB2 cursor that was used to page through Transaction Type reference records, releasing database resources once the current screen page has been populated. Any failure to cleanly close the cursor is captured as a database error to alert administrators of a system-level problem.

paragraphs.name: 9450-CLOSE-FORWARD-CURSOR-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the formal exit point of the forward cursor closing routine, serving as a structured return label after the DB2 cursor used to page through Transaction Type records has been closed. This paragraph exists to support clean structured programming flow within the paging and data retrieval process.

paragraphs.name: 9500-OPEN-BACKWARD-CURSOR
paragraphs.description: Opens a backward-scrolling database cursor to retrieve Transaction Type reference records in reverse order, enabling the administrator to page backwards through the list. If the cursor cannot be opened due to a database error, the failure is captured and a diagnostic message is prepared to inform the administrator that the backward navigation could not be performed.

paragraphs.name: 9500-OPEN-BACKWARD-CURSOR-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This is a formal exit point paragraph for the backward cursor opening routine, serving as a structured return marker in the transaction type list paging logic. It signals the end of the backward cursor initialisation process used when navigating to a previous page of transaction type records.

paragraphs.name: 9550-CLOSE-BACK-CURSOR
paragraphs.description: Releases the backward-paging database cursor used to retrieve Transaction Type records in reverse order, ensuring database resources are freed after the backward page navigation is complete. Any failure to close the cursor is captured and surfaced as a database error to prevent resource leaks and alert administrators to system issues.

paragraphs.name: 9550-CLOSE-BACK-CURSOR-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the backward cursor navigation routine used during paging through Transaction Type records. It also anchors the inclusion of shared DB2 database utility routines and the function key capture logic used throughout the maintenance workflow.

paragraphs.name: SEND-PLAIN-TEXT
paragraphs.description: Displays a plain-text system message to the bank administrator and terminates the current program interaction. This is used to communicate terminal-level feedback (such as errors or status notices) when a full formatted screen cannot or should not be rendered.

paragraphs.name: SEND-PLAIN-TEXT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the end of the debug text display routine used during development to output diagnostic messages to the screen. This paragraph is a placeholder exit point and is not part of the standard transaction type maintenance workflow.

paragraphs.name: SEND-LONG-TEXT
paragraphs.description: Displays a full-screen plain-text message to the bank administrator, typically used to communicate a critical system or error condition, then terminates the current program interaction and returns control to CICS.

paragraphs.name: SEND-LONG-TEXT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the end of the long text sending routine, serving as a structured exit point that allows other paragraphs to transfer control back to the calling workflow after screen messaging is complete.
